dedupe_keys.name: usgs pager global building inventory database building type fractions and occupancy by country

description: A global building inventory built by the USGS for PAGER (Prompt Assessment of Global Earthquakes for Response), its automated system that estimates fatalities and economic losses after significant earthquakes. Open-File Report 2008-1160 by Jaiswal and Wald, version 2.0 posted in October 2008, estimates for every country the fractions of building or dwelling types by PAGER structure type, their functional use, and average day and night occupancy, rating candidate sources by vintage and quality before choosing one. The database, Appendix VII of the report, has four tables covering urban or rural and residential or non-residential stock, with a release notes sheet. Coverage: all countries, one row per country in each table. Access: free download of the Excel appendix and the 103-page report. Licence: the report says the database is in the public domain, open to review and enhancement. Caveats: the inventory was a first pass from mixed sources of varying confidence, and the authors expected parts to be replaced by better data. Simulation uses: distributing exposed population across building types to estimate collapse casualties and losses in rapid earthquake impact models. Related records: the USGS PAGER earthquake impact alerts and the GEM global exposure model.
